school: Neoclassical Economics, Monetary Economics, International Economics
legacy: Gustav Cassel was one of the most influential economists of the early twentieth century and among the first economists to achieve truly international prominence. He played a major role in discussions about global monetary stability, exchange rates, and postwar economic reconstruction. His ideas helped governments, central banks, and economists understand how currencies relate to one another and how international financial systems function. Although some of his theories were later revised, his influence remains visible in international economics and monetary policy.
earlyLife: Cassel was born in Stockholm, Sweden. He initially studied engineering and mathematics before turning increasingly toward economics. This technical background shaped his distinctive analytical style, which emphasized clarity, logical structure, and practical applicability. During a period of rapid industrialization and expanding international trade, he became interested in understanding the forces governing prices, markets, and economic growth. These interests led him to become one of Scandinavia's most prominent economic thinkers.
scientificField: Economics, International Economics, Monetary Economics, Economic Theory
majorContributions: Cassel is best remembered for developing and popularizing the theory of Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), which argues that exchange rates tend to reflect differences in price levels between countries over the long run. This concept became one of the foundational ideas of international economics and continues to influence exchange-rate analysis today. He also contributed to theories of interest, capital, economic growth, and general equilibrium. Following the First World War, he became an influential advisor on monetary stabilization and international economic reconstruction, arguing for policies that would promote stable currencies and expanded international trade.
laterLife: During the interwar period, Cassel emerged as one of Europe's most widely read economists. His books and lectures attracted international audiences, and his opinions were frequently sought by governments and financial institutions. He participated actively in debates concerning inflation, reparations, exchange rates, and the future of the global economy. Even as economic theories evolved around him, he remained a prominent advocate of monetary stability, market coordination, and international economic cooperation.
whyImportant: Cassel is important because he helped establish many of the concepts used to analyze international monetary systems. His work on Purchasing Power Parity remains a fundamental reference point in discussions of currencies and exchange rates. He also contributed to the development of modern macroeconomic and international economic thought during a period when the world economy was becoming increasingly interconnected. His influence can still be seen in economic analysis conducted by governments, central banks, and international organizations.
